targets.description: Eradicate extreme poverty (below $1.25/day)
targets.article: Extreme poverty means surviving below the international poverty line of $2.15 a day. Billions remain trapped in destitution, concentrated in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. The poverty headcount ratio and poverty gap measure depth and prevalence. Ultra-poor households lack income, assets, and economic opportunity. Poverty eradication demands tackling the poverty trap through rural development, financial inclusion, and targeted transfers to the poorest of the poor. Multi-dimensional poverty indices capture deprivation in health, education, and living standards beyond income. Eliminating extreme poverty by 2030 requires accelerated, country-specific strategies.

targets.description: Reduce poverty by at least half in all dimensions
targets.article: National poverty lines define country-specific thresholds for relative poverty. Reducing poverty by at least half in all dimensions — income, food, health, education — requires targeting poor and vulnerable households across the bottom quintile. The multidimensional poverty index captures social and economic deprivation beyond income. The poverty gap and poverty incidence measure how deep and widespread hardship is. National poverty reduction strategies must integrate employment creation, social protection, and equitable service access so households can build lasting pathways out of poverty.

targets.description: Implement social protection systems and floors
targets.article: Social protection systems provide safety nets against poverty and vulnerability. Cash transfers — conditional or unconditional — deliver direct income to poor families. Social insurance schemes cover unemployment, disability, maternity, and old age through pensions and benefit programs. Food stamps and poverty grants protect households from shocks. Universal basic income proposals aim to extend coverage to all citizens. Social protection floors set minimum income and service guarantees across the lifecycle. Expanding welfare benefits and social assistance is critical to shielding the poorest from economic crises.

targets.description: Equal rights to economic resources, basic services, land and property
targets.article: Equal access to economic resources for the poor requires secure land rights and property rights. Land tenure security protects smallholders from eviction and enables investment. Microfinance and microcredit expand financial inclusion, giving poor households access to savings accounts and credit. Basic services — health, education, water — must reach the poorest. Financial services access through mobile banking narrows barriers for the unbanked. Agrarian reform and equitable land distribution reduce rural poverty. Economic rights for women and marginalised groups underpin inclusive poverty reduction strategies.

targets.description: Resilience of the poor to climate and economic shocks
targets.article: Poor and vulnerable communities face disproportionate exposure to climate shocks, natural disasters, and economic crises. Disaster risk reduction builds livelihood resilience among the ultra-poor. Adaptive capacity and shock absorption protect households from extreme weather, floods, droughts, and economic downturns. Climate exposure erodes savings and assets, deepening poverty traps. Community resilience programmes combine early warning systems, insurance schemes, and social protection. Resilient livelihoods for rural farmers require diversified income sources and climate-smart agriculture to withstand shocks without falling back into destitution.

targets.description: Mobilise resources for poverty eradication programmes
targets.article: Mobilising adequate financial resources for poverty eradication requires pro-poor fiscal policy and increased official development assistance (ODA) targeted at the poorest. Government spending on social programmes, rural infrastructure, and anti-poverty investment drives sustainable progress. Development aid, resource mobilisation, and domestic revenue collection must be directed toward poverty reduction strategies. International donors and multilateral institutions play a key role in funding poverty programs in least developed countries. Poverty program funding must be stable, transparent, and aligned with national development plans.

targets.description: Pro-poor policy frameworks based on development strategies
targets.article: Pro-poor policy frameworks embedded in national development plans ensure that economic growth benefits the poorest. Gender-responsive budgeting allocates public resources equitably. Poverty mainstreaming integrates anti-poverty measures across all government sectors. Inclusive development strategies prioritise equity, targeting marginalised groups. Evidence-based poverty policy frameworks align fiscal, social, and economic policies around poverty eradication. Country-owned strategies grounded in local development plans improve accountability and sustainability. Coherent anti-poverty governance combines regulation, service delivery, and community participation to reduce inequality and exclusion.

targets.description: End hunger and ensure access to food for all
targets.article: Hunger and food insecurity affect hundreds of millions globally. Famine, acute food crises, and chronic undernourishment persist in conflict zones and climate-vulnerable regions. Emergency food aid, food distribution, and food rationing address acute hunger. Food access requires affordable, nutritious food reaching all populations year-round. Famine early warning systems monitor food supply and alert to food emergencies. Starvation and food shortages disproportionately affect children and displaced populations. Zero hunger requires addressing both immediate food crises and structural food insecurity through resilient food systems.

targets.description: End all forms of malnutrition
targets.article: Malnutrition in all its forms — stunting, wasting, undernutrition, overweight, and micronutrient deficiencies — impairs child development and productivity. Acute malnutrition causes stunted growth and wasting among children under five. Anaemia, vitamin deficiency, and dietary diversity gaps persist in low-income countries. Obesity and overweight affect middle and high-income populations. Nutrition interventions including therapeutic feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and improved infant and young child feeding practices are critical. Childhood malnutrition drives long-term poverty and health burdens, demanding integrated nutrition programs across health and food systems.

targets.description: Double agricultural productivity of small-scale food producers
targets.article: Smallholder farmers, family farmers, and small-scale food producers generate most of the world's food yet earn poverty-level incomes. Doubling agricultural productivity of rural farmers requires closing the yield gap through improved seeds, inputs, and technology. Subsistence and peasant farmers need access to markets, land, credit, and extension services. Farm income growth and agrarian reform empower smallholders to invest. Smallholder productivity gains reduce rural poverty and strengthen food systems. Supporting artisanal and family farmers drives inclusive economic growth in rural economies.

targets.description: Sustainable food production systems and resilient agriculture
targets.article: Sustainable food production systems manage land, water, and biodiversity without depleting natural resources. Regenerative agriculture and agroecology restore soil health while maintaining yields. Resilient farming adapts to climate variability through drought-resistant crops and water conservation. Organic farming reduces chemical inputs and protects ecosystems. Climate-smart agriculture combines productivity with emission reduction. Sustainable farming practices protect freshwater resources, reduce erosion, and maintain ecosystem services. Food system resilience requires transitioning from industrial monoculture toward diversified, sustainable food production models.

targets.description: Genetic diversity of seeds, plants and animals
targets.article: Genetic diversity of seeds, plants, and animals underpins food security and agricultural adaptation. Seed banks, gene banks, and plant genetic resource collections preserve agrobiodiversity against climate change and crop failure. Local crop varieties and heritage seeds carry resistance traits essential for breeding resilient cultivars. Animal genetic resources diversity ensures livestock can adapt to changing conditions. The loss of crop diversity and traditional seed systems threatens food system resilience. Protecting agrobiodiversity through community seed conservation and gene bank management safeguards future food production capacity.

targets.description: Investment in rural infrastructure and agricultural research
targets.article: Investment in rural infrastructure — irrigation systems, rural roads, storage facilities, and electricity — is essential for agricultural productivity. Agricultural research and development of crop technology drive yield improvements. Extension services deliver knowledge and inputs to farmers. Irrigation infrastructure expands cultivated area and reduces weather dependence. Farming technology adoption raises efficiency among smallholders. Rural roads reduce post-harvest losses and connect farmers to markets. Sustained public and private agricultural investment in developing countries closes the productivity gap and improves food security.

targets.description: Correct and prevent trade restrictions in world agricultural markets
targets.article: Distortions in global agricultural trade — export subsidies, tariffs, and import restrictions — undermine food security in developing countries. WTO agriculture negotiations aim to correct unfair trade policies that depress commodity prices for smallholder farmers. Agricultural export restrictions and food trade barriers disrupt global food markets. Removing market-distorting subsidies in rich countries levels the playing field for agricultural producers in the Global South. Equitable food trade policy supports rural livelihoods and improves food availability in import-dependent countries.

targets.description: Stable food commodity markets and limit extreme price volatility
targets.article: Extreme food price volatility destabilises livelihoods, triggers food crises, and undermines nutrition. Commodity market speculation and supply shocks cause food price spikes that hit poor consumers hardest. Food inflation and staple crop price surges reduce dietary quality and increase hunger. Cereal and grain price instability disrupts smallholder incomes. Stabilising food commodity markets through reserves, trade coordination, and transparent information systems limits extreme price volatility. Governance of food markets must protect against speculation and ensure stable, affordable food for all.

targets.description: Reduce global maternal mortality ratio
targets.article: Maternal mortality remains unacceptably high in low-income countries, caused by obstetric complications, haemorrhage, and lack of skilled birth attendants. Reducing the maternal mortality ratio requires universal access to antenatal care, safe delivery, and postnatal care. Midwives, obstetricians, and emergency obstetric services prevent maternal deaths. Caesarean section access and management of pregnancy complications save lives. Obstetric fistula and sepsis represent preventable causes of maternal death. Strengthening maternal health systems in fragile and conflict-affected settings is critical to achieving significant reductions in maternal mortality.

targets.description: End preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5
targets.article: Child mortality and infant mortality remain leading causes of preventable death globally. Neonatal deaths in the first 28 days account for nearly half of under-five mortality. Childhood pneumonia, diarrhoea, malaria, and vaccine-preventable diseases drive child mortality. Immunisation for children, oral rehydration therapy, and nutrition interventions are highly effective. Under-five and infant death rates have declined but remain high in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Child survival requires community health workers, postnatal care, and quality healthcare access to end preventable deaths among newborns and young children.

targets.description: End AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases
targets.article: HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis (TB), malaria, hepatitis, and neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) continue to burden low-income countries. Communicable disease epidemics including cholera, dengue, Ebola, mpox, and drug-resistant infections demand surveillance and rapid response. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens to undermine treatment of infectious diseases. HIV treatment, TB case detection, malaria prevention, and NTD elimination programmes have made progress but funding gaps remain. Disease surveillance, contact tracing, and pathogen monitoring are essential to prevent outbreaks from becoming epidemics.

targets.description: Reduce premature mortality from non-communicable diseases
targets.article: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) — cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, stroke, and chronic respiratory illness — cause the majority of premature deaths globally. Hypertension, obesity-related disease, and unhealthy diets drive NCD burden. Mental health disorders including depression, anxiety, and psychosis are major causes of disability. Suicide and self-harm require psychosocial support and mental health services. Reducing premature NCD mortality demands improved screening, essential medicines, and health system capacity. Mental health care integration into primary health systems remains critically underfunded in most countries.

targets.description: Strengthen prevention and treatment of substance abuse
targets.article: Substance abuse — alcohol addiction, opioid dependency, and illicit drug use — causes significant mortality, disability, and social harm. Drug treatment and rehabilitation services are insufficient in most countries. Harm reduction approaches including needle exchange, opioid substitution therapy, and naloxone distribution save lives. Alcohol abuse drives violence, road deaths, and liver disease. Drug dependency treatment requires integrated health, social, and criminal justice responses. Narcotics trafficking fuels addiction crises globally. Prevention, treatment, and recovery support for substance use disorders must be expanded urgently.

targets.description: Halve global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents
targets.article: Road traffic accidents kill over a million people annually and injure tens of millions more. Traffic fatalities disproportionately affect pedestrians, cyclists, and motorcyclists in low-income countries. Drunk driving, speeding, and failure to wear seatbelts or helmets are leading causes of road deaths. Road safety engineering, speed limits, and traffic law enforcement reduce crash mortality. Pedestrian safety infrastructure and road injury prevention save lives. Halving global traffic deaths requires investment in safe road design, vehicle standards, and driver education in countries where traffic injury rates are highest.

targets.description: Universal access to sexual and reproductive health care services
targets.article: Sexual and reproductive health care — family planning, contraception, antenatal care, and safe delivery — is a fundamental right. Reproductive health services prevent maternal mortality and unintended pregnancies. Contraceptive access empowers women to plan families and pursue education and work. Safe abortion access reduces maternal deaths from unsafe procedures. SRHR includes gynaecological care, menstrual health, and treatment of reproductive infections. Reproductive rights and reproductive autonomy underpin women's full participation in society. Universal access to reproductive health services remains unmet for millions of women in developing countries.

targets.description: Achieve universal health coverage
targets.article: Universal health coverage (UHC) means every person receives quality health services without financial hardship. Healthcare access requires hospitals, clinics, community health centres, and trained health workers. Essential medicines, diagnostics, and health insurance prevent catastrophic out-of-pocket health spending. Health systems strengthening addresses chronic underfunding, medicine shortages, and workforce gaps. Public health infrastructure in low-income countries collapses under disease burden. Health financing through insurance schemes and government health expenditure drives coverage expansion. UHC remains the foundation for all health goal achievement.

targets.description: Reduce deaths from hazardous chemicals and environmental pollution
targets.article: Pollution-related deaths from air pollution, contaminated water, hazardous chemicals, and toxic substances kill millions annually. Lead poisoning damages children's cognitive development and causes premature death. Indoor air pollution from cooking fires causes respiratory disease. Chemical exposure in workplaces and communities creates long-term health burdens. Environmental health risks — including industrial pollution and pesticide contamination — disproportionately affect poor and marginalised communities. Reducing contamination health impacts requires environmental regulation, clean technology, and stronger chemical management standards globally.

targets.description: Strengthen implementation of WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control
targets.article: Tobacco use is the world's leading preventable cause of death. The Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) sets international standards for smoking regulation. Tobacco taxes reduce consumption and fund health services. Smoking bans in public places, workplaces, and transport protect non-smokers from second-hand smoke. Plain packaging, advertising restrictions, and smoking cessation programmes reduce tobacco use. Nicotine addiction and cigarette dependence require sustained policy action. Anti-tobacco measures save lives and reduce healthcare costs. Comprehensive tobacco control implementation remains incomplete in many low- and middle-income countries.

targets.description: Support research and development of vaccines and medicines
targets.article: Vaccines and essential medicines save lives but remain inaccessible in many developing countries due to cost and supply barriers. Vaccination campaigns and immunisation coverage prevent measles, polio, meningitis, and other preventable diseases. Vaccine equity ensures equitable vaccine distribution across income groups and geographies. The TRIPS agreement and compulsory licensing affect medicine access in low-income countries. Drug research and development for neglected diseases remains underfunded. Vaccine rollout programmes require cold chains, trained staff, and community trust. Access to essential medicines for developing countries demands global cooperation.

targets.description: Substantially increase health workforce and capacity
targets.article: Health workforce shortages — doctors, nurses, midwives, and community health workers — cripple health systems in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Brain drain depletes trained medical staff from low-income countries to richer nations. Health worker deployment to rural and remote areas remains inadequate. Medical training institutions lack capacity to produce sufficient graduates. Nurse shortages leave hospitals dangerously understaffed. Physician density and midwife availability are critical indicators of health system capacity. Scaling up health staff through medical education investment and retention incentives is essential for achieving universal health coverage.

targets.description: Strengthen national capacity for health security and risk reduction
targets.article: Health security requires national capacity to detect, prevent, and respond to epidemic and pandemic threats. International Health Regulations (IHR) set standards for surveillance and response. Pandemic preparedness — stockpiles, protocols, and trained responders — limits mortality when outbreaks occur. Biosecurity protects against deliberate and natural biological threats. Early warning epidemic systems enable rapid containment. Health emergency preparedness covers laboratory capacity, port-of-entry controls, and risk communication. Outbreak response capacity was exposed as dangerously inadequate during COVID-19, revealing urgent gaps in global health security.

targets.description: Free, equitable and quality primary and secondary education
targets.article: Universal primary and secondary education must be free, equitable, and of quality. School enrolment, attendance, and completion rates measure progress, but learning outcomes matter more than seat time. Learning poverty — inability to read by age 10 — affects hundreds of millions. School dropout, especially among girls, remains high in fragile states. Out-of-school children represent a global education crisis. Secondary education completion drives long-term economic mobility. Quality of teaching, curriculum, and learning environment determines whether education translates into skills. Eliminating learning poverty requires targeted investment in school quality.

targets.description: Equal access to quality early childhood development and pre-primary education
targets.article: Early childhood education and care lays the cognitive, social, and emotional foundations for lifelong learning. Pre-primary education, preschool, and kindergarten programmes improve school readiness and reduce learning gaps. Early childhood development (ECD) encompasses nutrition, stimulation, and family support for children under six. Nursery schools and community-based childcare provide developmental environments for young children. Investment in early learning yields the highest returns of any educational intervention. Child development outcomes depend on quality early childhood care accessible to all socio-economic groups.

targets.description: Equal access to affordable technical, vocational and higher education
targets.article: Higher education, technical and vocational education (TVET), and tertiary institutions must be accessible and affordable to all. University fees and financial barriers exclude students from low-income households. Vocational training and technical education prepare youth for skilled employment and entrepreneurship. College access for women, rural, and disadvantaged populations drives economic inclusion. Affordable education policies — subsidised fees, scholarships, and student loans — widen participation. Tertiary education quality and graduate employability determine whether higher education investment translates into economic growth and individual mobility.

targets.description: Increase youth and adults with relevant technical and vocational skills
targets.article: Youth and adults need relevant technical, vocational, and digital skills for decent work. Skills training programmes address the skills gap between graduates and labour market demand. Digital literacy and digital skills are prerequisites for the modern economy. STEM education prepares workers for science, technology, and innovation roles. Vocational skills development through apprenticeships and TVET improves employability. Workforce skills deficits limit productivity in both developed and developing economies. Lifelong learning and continuous reskilling programmes enable workers to adapt to technological change and automation.

targets.description: Eliminate gender disparities in education
targets.article: Gender disparities in education persist through unequal enrolment, completion, and learning outcomes for girls. Inclusive education systems serve students with disabilities, indigenous children, and other vulnerable groups. Girl enrolment and school retention depend on eliminating fees, providing safety, and addressing gender-based violence in schools. Education inequality between rural and urban, rich and poor, and different ethnic groups requires targeted policy. Disability education access through accessible schools and specialised support is a right. Ending discrimination in education demands affirmative measures and gender parity monitoring.

targets.description: Universal youth and adult literacy and numeracy
targets.article: Illiteracy and innumeracy trap adults in poverty and exclusion. Universal youth and adult literacy means every person can read, write, and perform basic calculations. Functional illiteracy — inability to use reading and writing in daily life — is widespread among adults in low-income countries. Adult literacy programmes and literacy training reach those who missed schooling. Reading ability and writing ability are foundational for health, civic participation, and economic productivity. Youth literacy rates have improved but adult literacy gaps persist, particularly among older women with no schooling.

targets.description: Education for sustainable development and global citizenship
targets.article: Education for sustainable development (ESD) equips learners with knowledge, values, and skills to address climate change, biodiversity loss, and inequality. Global citizenship education fosters respect for human rights, cultural diversity, and democratic values. Peace education reduces conflict and promotes reconciliation. Environmental education builds ecological literacy and sustainable behaviours. Human rights education supports justice and accountability. Sustainability education challenges consumption patterns and promotes responsible lifestyles. Integrating ESD across curricula prepares students to navigate global challenges and contribute to just, sustainable societies.

targets.description: Build inclusive and safe learning facilities
targets.article: Safe, inclusive, and well-equipped learning facilities are prerequisites for quality education. School infrastructure — classrooms, libraries, laboratories — must be built and maintained. Safe schools protect students from violence, harassment, and natural disasters. WASH in schools — water, sanitation, and hygiene facilities — supports girls' attendance. Disability-friendly schools with ramps, accessible toilets, and learning aids ensure inclusion for students with disabilities. School safety policies protect children from armed attacks. Investment in school construction and rehabilitation must prioritise underserved rural and marginalised communities.

targets.description: Expand scholarships for developing countries
targets.article: Scholarships and educational grants expand access to higher education and vocational training for students from developing countries and disadvantaged backgrounds. Fellowships and academic bursaries fund postgraduate study and research capacity. Study abroad programmes build international skills and networks. Higher education grants target students from least developed countries, small island states, and conflict-affected regions. Student grants reduce financial barriers to tertiary education for low-income families. Expanding scholarship availability supports the development of skilled professionals in sectors critical to sustainable development.

targets.description: Increase supply of qualified teachers
targets.article: Teacher shortages undermine education quality worldwide, particularly in rural and fragile settings. Teacher training and professional development improve pedagogy and learning outcomes. Qualified teacher recruitment and deployment to underserved areas requires financial incentives. Teacher quality — subject knowledge, classroom management, and instructional methods — determines student achievement. Teaching workforce expansion through pre-service and in-service training programmes is essential. Teacher qualification standards and performance evaluation improve accountability. Addressing teacher shortages demands increased education budgets, competitive salaries, and sustainable pipelines of trained professionals.

targets.description: End all forms of discrimination against women and girls
targets.article: Gender discrimination denies women and girls equal rights in law, policy, and practice. Legal equality for women requires abolishing discriminatory laws and enforcing equal protection. Gender inequality in education, employment, political participation, and inheritance perpetuates poverty and exclusion. Women's rights include equal access to justice, property, and economic resources. Anti-discrimination legislation and gender parity policies must be backed by enforcement mechanisms. Girls' rights to education, health, and physical safety are routinely violated. Achieving gender equality demands transforming legal frameworks, social norms, and institutional practices.

targets.description: Eliminate violence against women and girls
targets.article: Violence against women and girls — including domestic violence, sexual assault, intimate partner violence, femicide, and trafficking — is a global human rights crisis. Gender-based violence (GBV) affects one in three women. Sexual harassment in workplaces, public spaces, and online silences and excludes women. Trafficking of women and sexual exploitation remain widespread despite legal prohibitions. Violence against girls includes child sexual abuse, online exploitation, and coerced marriage. Eliminating GBV requires legal accountability, survivor support services, changing harmful masculinity norms, and ending impunity for perpetrators.

targets.description: Eliminate harmful practices (child marriage, FGM)
targets.article: Child marriage forces girls into early union before adulthood, denying education, health, and autonomy. Forced marriage and early marriage trap girls in poverty cycles. Female genital mutilation (FGM) is a harmful practice violating girls' bodily integrity and causing lasting physical and psychological harm. Female circumcision persists in communities across sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East, and parts of Asia. Honour killing and other harmful traditional practices target women who defy gender norms. Eliminating these practices requires legal frameworks, community engagement, education, and alternative rites of passage programmes.

targets.description: Value unpaid care and domestic work
targets.article: Unpaid care work and domestic work — childcare, cooking, cleaning, elder care — falls disproportionately on women and girls, limiting their time, education, and economic opportunities. The care economy is undervalued in national accounts despite its essential contribution. Shared responsibility for household duties between men and women reduces the caregiving burden on women. Women's domestic work subsidises the formal economy. Public investment in childcare infrastructure and parental leave policies redistributes care responsibilities. Recognising and valuing unpaid care work is fundamental to achieving gender economic equality.

targets.description: Full participation and equal leadership opportunities for women
targets.article: Women's political participation and leadership remain far below parity globally. Women in parliament, government cabinets, and senior management positions are underrepresented due to systemic barriers and gender discrimination. Women in decision-making roles improve governance outcomes and policy priorities. Equal pay and the gender pay gap persist across all sectors and income levels. Women's representation in political parties, boardrooms, and public institutions must increase. Quotas, affirmative action, and mentorship programmes accelerate women's leadership. Women's empowerment in economic and political life drives development for entire communities.

targets.description: Universal access to reproductive rights and health
targets.article: Reproductive rights and sexual health are fundamental to women's autonomy and wellbeing. Universal access to reproductive health services — contraception, family planning, menstrual health, and fertility care — remains unmet for millions. Contraceptive access and reproductive autonomy enable women to control their own bodies and life choices. Abortion rights and safe abortion services prevent maternal death from unsafe procedures. Period poverty and menstrual hygiene management affect girls' school attendance. Reproductive health service provision must be free from coercion and discrimination, grounded in comprehensive sexuality education.

targets.description: Equal rights to economic resources, property and financial services
targets.article: Women's economic empowerment requires equal rights to land, property, and financial services. Women's land rights and property ownership enable investment and wealth accumulation. Discriminatory inheritance laws deny women assets passed to male heirs. Women's financial inclusion through bank accounts, credit, and mobile money reduces economic dependence and vulnerability. Women's land titling programmes improve family nutrition and children's education. Equal access to economic resources for women is both a rights issue and a development imperative. Legal reform alone is insufficient without enforcement and community-level norm change.

targets.description: Enhance use of technology to promote women's empowerment
targets.article: Technology and digital tools can accelerate women's empowerment when access is equitable. Mobile phones enable women to access information, financial services, markets, and support networks. The digital gender divide — fewer women than men using the internet and mobile technology — limits women's economic and social participation. ICT access for women in rural areas opens education, entrepreneurship, and healthcare opportunities. Women's internet access and digital skills training close participation gaps. Technology empowerment of women requires addressing affordability, safety, and cultural barriers that restrict women's use of digital technologies.

targets.description: Adopt policies and legislation for gender equality
targets.article: Gender equality requires enforceable legal frameworks, policies, and institutional mechanisms. Gender equality laws criminalise discrimination and harassment. Quota systems and affirmative action policies for women in parliament and corporate boards accelerate representation. Gender mainstreaming integrates gender analysis into all government planning and budgeting. Gender-responsive budgeting allocates public resources to close gender gaps. Anti-discrimination policy in employment, education, and health protects women's rights. Monitoring gender legislation implementation and tracking gender indicators hold governments accountable for progress toward equality.

targets.description: Universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water
targets.article: Safe and affordable drinking water is a human right yet billions lack access. Clean water supply through piped connections, boreholes, hand pumps, and water kiosks serves communities without reliable household water. Groundwater, aquifers, and water tables supply rural populations. Potable water quality prevents waterborne disease. Water access disparities between urban and rural areas remain stark. Water point construction and maintenance keep communities supplied during dry seasons. Universal water coverage requires sustained investment, governance, and operation of water infrastructure to ensure households receive safe water consistently.

targets.description: Access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene
targets.article: Sanitation and hygiene access prevent disease and protect dignity. Open defecation contaminates water sources and spreads diarrhoea, cholera, and typhoid. Latrine and toilet construction must be accompanied by behaviour change for open defecation-free communities. Handwashing with soap at critical moments breaks disease transmission. WASH programmes — water, sanitation, and hygiene — deliver integrated services to schools, health facilities, and households. Menstrual hygiene management in schools keeps girls attending. School sanitation provision directly affects children's health and learning. Achieving universal sanitation demands sustained investment and community mobilisation.

targets.description: Improve water quality, wastewater treatment and safe reuse
targets.article: Wastewater treatment protects public health and water ecosystems. Sewage and effluent discharged untreated contaminates rivers, lakes, and coastal waters. Water treatment plants, sewer systems, and sewerage networks remove pathogens and pollutants. Urban drainage infrastructure manages stormwater and prevents flooding. Water recycling and safe reuse of treated wastewater conserves scarce resources. Drinking water quality monitoring detects contamination before it harms populations. Freshwater pollution from agriculture, industry, and sewage degrading water quality is a global crisis requiring investment in treatment infrastructure and regulation.

targets.description: Substantially increase water-use efficiency
targets.article: Water scarcity affects over two billion people globally. Water stress, water deficits, and freshwater shortages intensify with climate change, population growth, and agricultural demand. Water-use efficiency in irrigation, industry, and households reduces pressure on scarce freshwater. Desalination provides alternative water sources in arid coastal regions. Rainwater harvesting captures and stores rainfall for agricultural and household use. Water productivity — output per unit of water — improves with technology and crop selection. Addressing water insecurity demands integrated water demand management and efficiency standards across all sectors.

targets.description: Implement integrated water resources management
targets.article: Integrated water resources management (IWRM) coordinates water use across sectors, jurisdictions, and stakeholders. Transboundary water governance manages shared rivers, lakes, and aquifers between countries. Water policy and water law establish rights, allocations, and dispute resolution mechanisms. Watershed management and river basin governance protect upstream-downstream linkages. Water governance institutions coordinate irrigation, municipal, industrial, and environmental water use. Managing shared water resources requires negotiated agreements, data sharing, and cooperative institutions across national borders and sectoral interests.

targets.description: Protect and restore water-related ecosystems
targets.article: Water-related ecosystems — wetlands, rivers, lakes, and aquifers — provide essential services including flood regulation, water purification, and biodiversity habitat. Wetland restoration and river restoration recover degraded freshwater ecosystems. Aquifer protection preserves groundwater quality and recharge. Freshwater ecosystem conservation maintains biodiversity and water supply for communities. Wetland conservation reduces flood risk and sequesters carbon. Lake restoration addresses eutrophication and pollution. Protecting water-related ecosystems requires integrating environmental flows into water management and preventing encroachment and drainage of natural wetlands.

targets.description: Expand international cooperation for water and sanitation
targets.article: International cooperation in water and sanitation finance is essential for reaching underserved populations in developing countries. WASH funding from development aid, multilateral institutions, and bilateral donors builds water infrastructure. Water aid and sanitation cooperation support country programmes in least developed nations. Capacity building for water management professionals strengthens institutional performance. International cooperation delivers technical assistance for water governance reform. Financing mechanisms for water infrastructure must reach rural and peri-urban areas where access gaps are largest and local government capacity is weakest.

targets.description: Support local community participation in water and sanitation management
targets.article: Community participation in water and sanitation management builds ownership and sustainability. Local water governance through water user associations, community committees, and village water boards maintains infrastructure after installation. Participatory water management ensures services reflect community needs and priorities. Community sanitation programmes engage households in planning and managing toilet facilities. Women's participation in water committees improves service quality and equity. Decentralised water management supported by local government capacity strengthens accountability and long-term service delivery in rural and peri-urban communities.

targets.description: Universal access to modern energy services
targets.article: Energy access for all requires extending electricity and clean cooking to unserved populations. Nearly a billion people lack electricity access, concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Off-grid solar systems, mini-grids, and grid extension reach remote communities. Energy poverty traps households in low productivity and poor health from cooking smoke. Clean cooking — LPG, biogas, improved cookstoves — replaces polluting open fires. Rural electrification enables lighting, refrigeration, and productive use. Power outages and electricity shortages disrupt businesses and healthcare. Energy for all is foundational to achieving all other sustainable development goals.

targets.description: Increase share of renewable energy
targets.article: Renewable energy — solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, and biomass — must replace fossil fuels to decarbonise electricity systems. Solar panels, wind turbines, and solar farms are driving rapid clean energy expansion. The energy transition from coal, gas, and oil to clean electricity is accelerating globally but not fast enough. Renewable energy share of total energy consumption must increase dramatically. Wind energy and hydropower already provide significant generation capacity. Green energy investment creates jobs and reduces emissions. Clean energy transition requires grid integration, storage, and policy support for renewables to displace fossil fuels.

targets.description: Double global rate of energy efficiency improvement
targets.article: Energy efficiency improvements reduce consumption, costs, and emissions across buildings, transport, and industry. Energy saving through efficient appliances, insulation, and industrial processes lowers energy demand. Battery storage and energy storage technologies enable better integration of variable renewables. Building energy standards and efficiency regulations cut consumption in new construction. Transport energy efficiency improvements through electric vehicles and public transit reduce oil dependence. Industrial energy efficiency gains lower production costs and emissions. Doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement requires stronger standards, audits, and financial incentives.

targets.description: Enhance international cooperation on clean energy research
targets.article: Clean energy research, investment, and international cooperation accelerate the energy transition. Renewable energy investment must reach trillions annually to meet climate targets. Energy financing through multilateral development banks and private capital funds clean power projects. Technology transfer supports developing countries in adopting clean energy. Just energy transition programmes protect fossil fuel workers and communities from economic disruption. Coal phase-out and fossil fuel phase-down require political commitment and financial support. Climate funds including the Green Climate Fund channel money to clean energy projects in vulnerable developing countries.

targets.description: Expand infrastructure and upgrade technology for modern energy services
targets.article: Expanding clean energy infrastructure in developing countries and upgrading energy technology are critical for modern energy service access. Grid expansion and mini-grid investment bring electricity to underserved regions. Energy infrastructure development requires sustained capital investment and technical capacity. Developing country energy supply gaps leave hospitals, schools, and businesses without reliable power. Fuel shortages and gas crises disrupt economic activity. Energy technology upgrades improve efficiency and reliability of power systems. Building sustainable energy infrastructure requires long-term planning, regulation, and international partnerships.

targets.description: Sustain per capita economic growth
targets.article: Sustained per capita economic growth drives poverty reduction and rising living standards. GDP growth and productivity growth determine whether countries can fund development. Least developed countries require GDP growth of at least 7 percent annually to transform their economies. Economic development and inclusive growth distribute gains broadly across income groups. Economic diversification reduces dependence on commodities and external shocks. Per capita income growth narrows absolute poverty even without redistributive policy. Sustaining growth amid climate change, conflict, and pandemic disruption demands resilient macroeconomic management.

targets.description: Achieve higher economic productivity through diversification and innovation
targets.article: Higher economic productivity through diversification, innovation, and technology upgrading drives long-term growth. Industrial upgrading moves economies from low-value commodity exports toward manufacturing and services. Economic diversification reduces commodity dependency and vulnerability. Value added in agriculture, manufacturing, and services grows through technology adoption and skills development. Economic innovation — new products, processes, and business models — improves productivity. Productivity growth requires investment in research, education, and infrastructure. Diversified, innovation-driven economies generate more jobs and higher wages than resource-dependent ones.

targets.description: Promote development-oriented policies for entrepreneurship
targets.article: Entrepreneurship, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and the informal economy generate most jobs in developing countries. Business development support — incubators, mentoring, and finance — helps small enterprises grow. Micro-enterprise and self-employment enable the poor to earn income without formal job markets. Informal economy workers lack labour protections and social security. Startup ecosystems drive innovation and employment creation. SME finance, registration simplification, and market access policies formalise businesses. Development-oriented policies for entrepreneurship must reduce barriers and provide support for micro and small businesses to expand.

targets.description: Improve resource efficiency in consumption and production
targets.article: Resource efficiency in consumption and production decouples economic growth from environmental degradation. Material footprint measures the total resources consumed by an economy. Decoupling GDP growth from resource use and pollution is essential for sustainable development. Unsustainable consumption patterns in high-income countries drive global resource overuse. Economic efficiency improvements reduce waste and lower production costs. Circular economy approaches keep materials in use longer. Resource-efficient industrial processes cut raw material demand. Sustainable economic growth must achieve more output per unit of natural resource input while protecting ecological boundaries.

targets.description: Full and productive employment and decent work for all
targets.article: Full and productive employment with decent work means every person can earn a living wage in safe, dignified conditions. Unemployment and joblessness trap households in poverty. Job creation requires investment, economic growth, and labour market policies. Decent jobs provide fair wages, social protection, and stable contracts. The gender pay gap and wage inequality deny equal pay for equal work. Living wage and minimum wage standards set floors below which pay cannot fall. Quality employment in formal sectors with decent work conditions is the foundation for economic security and social dignity for all workers.

targets.description: Reduce proportion of youth not in employment, education or training
targets.article: Youth unemployment, underemployment, and the proportion of young people not in employment, education, or training (NEET) represent wasted human capital and social risk. Informal economy workers — particularly youth — lack job security, benefits, and protection. Precarious work including zero-hour contracts and gig economy jobs offer no stability. Youth employment policies, apprenticeships, and school-to-work transitions support young people into productive roles. Reducing NEET rates requires coordinated education, training, and labour market interventions. Informal sector workers need pathways toward formalisation with decent working conditions.

targets.description: End forced labour, modern slavery, human trafficking and child labour
targets.article: Child labour, forced labour, modern slavery, and human trafficking deprive millions of children and adults of their freedom and development. Child labour in agriculture, mining, and domestic service perpetuates intergenerational poverty. The worst forms of child labour include hazardous work and child soldiering. Debt bondage and bonded labour trap workers in servitude. Modern slavery in supply chains of global companies remains widespread. Forced labour trafficking exploits migrants and displaced persons. Labour trafficking and sweatshop conditions violate fundamental rights. Ending child labour requires education, social protection, and enforcement against exploitative employers.

targets.description: Protect labour rights and safe working environments
targets.article: Labour rights and safe working conditions are fundamental human rights. Worker exploitation, wage theft, and unsafe working environments harm millions of workers globally. Occupational safety standards and labour inspections prevent workplace accidents and deaths. Trade unions and collective bargaining protect workers' rights and wages. Migrant worker exploitation and migrant labour abuses — unpaid wages, confiscated passports, forced overtime — are rampant in construction, domestic service, and agriculture. Labour standards enforcement, workers' unions, and strike action protect rights. Global supply chain transparency and corporate accountability are essential to uphold labour rights.

targets.description: Promote sustainable tourism and local culture
targets.article: Sustainable tourism creates jobs and economic value while protecting natural and cultural heritage. Ecotourism and cultural tourism generate income for local communities and incentivise conservation. Tourism jobs in hotels, guiding, transport, and hospitality employ millions, particularly in small island states and coastal economies. Tourism sector management must minimise environmental impacts and respect local cultures. Sustainable tourism certification and impact monitoring improve industry practices. Over-tourism in popular destinations degrades environments and communities. Community-based tourism distributes benefits broadly and supports traditional livelihoods alongside economic development.

targets.description: Strengthen domestic financial institutions
targets.article: Financial inclusion connects unbanked populations to banking, savings, credit, and insurance. Mobile banking and fintech services reach populations without formal bank accounts. Remittances from migrant workers are a critical income source for developing country households, requiring affordable money transfer infrastructure. Microfinance institutions provide small loans enabling poor entrepreneurs to start businesses. Broadening access to financial services — accounts, digital payments, and credit — reduces economic exclusion. Strengthening domestic financial institutions builds stable credit markets that support economic growth and investment.

targets.description: Increase Aid for Trade support for developing countries
targets.article: Aid for Trade strengthens the capacity of developing countries to participate in global trade. Trade assistance programmes fund customs modernisation, logistics infrastructure, and export competitiveness. Trade capacity building helps least developed countries diversify exports and integrate into supply chains. Trade development support from multilateral institutions assists small economies in overcoming structural barriers. Aid for Trade improves behind-the-border conditions, reducing transaction costs and connecting farmers and businesses to international markets. Scaling up trade-related development finance is essential for export-led growth in vulnerable economies.

targets.description: Develop global strategy for youth employment
targets.article: A global strategy for youth employment coordinates national policies, training programmes, and labour market reforms to address youth unemployment. ILO youth employment initiatives promote apprenticeships, internships, and school-to-work transition programmes. Youth job training equips young people with skills demanded by employers. Youth employment strategy integrates education, vocational training, entrepreneurship support, and social protection. Addressing youth unemployment requires collaboration between governments, businesses, and educational institutions. Young people in developing countries face structural barriers to formal employment that dedicated policy and international support must overcome.

targets.description: Develop quality, reliable and sustainable infrastructure
targets.article: Reliable and sustainable infrastructure — roads, bridges, railways, ports, and airports — underpins economic development and connectivity. Infrastructure gaps in developing countries raise transport costs and isolate communities. Road construction, highway networks, and transport infrastructure link producers to markets and workers to jobs. Sustainable infrastructure resilient to climate change withstands floods, earthquakes, and extreme weather. Logistics and supply chain infrastructure reduce trade costs. The infrastructure deficit in sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and small island states demands massive investment from governments, multilateral banks, and private capital.

targets.description: Promote inclusive and sustainable industrialisation
targets.article: Inclusive and sustainable industrialisation generates employment, income, and structural economic transformation. Manufacturing sector development creates jobs and builds productive capacity. Industrial parks, special economic zones, and industrial zones attract investment and cluster complementary businesses. Industrial output growth drives economic diversification beyond commodity dependence. Industrialisation in developing countries requires trade policy, infrastructure, skills, and technology. Industrial capacity building for least developed countries supports their transition from agriculture-dependent to manufacturing-based economies. Inclusive industrialisation benefits women, youth, and marginalised groups through expanded formal employment.

targets.description: Increase access of small enterprises to financial services
targets.article: Small enterprises and micro-businesses struggle to access the financing they need to grow. SME financing through bank loans, microfinance, and equity capital is often unaffordable or unavailable in developing countries. Credit access for small businesses requires collateral-free lending, credit guarantees, and fintech innovations. SME loans enable equipment purchase, inventory expansion, and hiring. Business credit markets in low-income countries are shallow, expensive, and biased toward large firms. Strengthening financial systems to serve small enterprise finance needs — including women-owned businesses — drives inclusive economic growth.

targets.description: Upgrade infrastructure with clean and environmentally sound technologies
targets.article: Industrial pollution and industrial emissions degrade air, water, and soil, harming health and ecosystems. Upgrading infrastructure with clean and environmentally sound technologies reduces industrial environmental impact. Green manufacturing processes cut emissions and waste from production. Clean technology adoption by factories and industrial facilities improves resource efficiency. Industrial efficiency standards lower energy and material consumption. Retrofitting existing industrial plants with cleaner technologies reduces legacy pollution. Decarbonising heavy industry — steel, cement, chemicals — requires breakthrough clean technologies and supportive policy frameworks.

targets.description: Enhance scientific research and upgrade technological capabilities
targets.article: Scientific research and technological innovation drive long-term economic growth and problem-solving capacity. Research and development (R&D) spending by governments and businesses generates the discoveries and technologies needed for sustainable development. Innovation ecosystems — tech hubs, science parks, startup incubators — cluster talent and capital. Patent protection and intellectual property systems incentivise innovation. University-industry partnerships accelerate technology commercialisation. Science capacity in developing countries must be strengthened to reduce dependence on imported technology. Increasing R&D investment as a share of GDP is a key indicator of innovation commitment.

targets.description: Facilitate sustainable infrastructure development in developing countries
targets.article: Sustainable infrastructure development in developing countries requires international financial and technical support. Infrastructure financing from multilateral development banks, bilateral donors, and private investors funds roads, energy, and digital systems. Regional integration projects — corridors, power pools, internet cables — build connectivity across borders. Connectivity infrastructure reduces trade costs and supports economic integration in fragile and landlocked developing states. Developing country infrastructure gaps demand concessional finance, blended finance, and public-private partnerships. Technical assistance supports planning and procurement of large infrastructure projects.

targets.description: Support domestic technology development and industrial diversification
targets.article: Domestic technology development and industrial diversification reduce dependence on imported technologies and single commodity exports. Technology transfer from advanced to developing economies builds local innovation capacity. Domestic industrial policy supports local firms to develop manufacturing competencies. Technology policy and manufacturing policy create conditions for firms to climb value chains. Local content requirements and industrial diversification strategies grow productive sectors beyond extractive industries. Support for domestic technology development requires investment in education, skills, and innovation infrastructure alongside open trade regimes.

targets.description: Significantly increase access to ICT and internet
targets.article: Internet access and digital connectivity are essential infrastructure for the modern economy. The digital divide excludes billions from digital services, commerce, and information. Broadband access — fibre optic, wireless, and satellite — must reach rural and remote communities. Last-mile connectivity closes gaps where infrastructure is absent. Rural internet expansion requires subsidies and universal service obligations. Mobile networks and 4G/5G coverage extend digital access to underserved populations. ICT access enables e-government, digital banking, and online education. Undersea cables and telecommunications infrastructure form the backbone of global digital connectivity.

targets.description: Achieve income growth of the bottom 40 percent
targets.article: Income inequality between the top and bottom of the wealth distribution is rising globally. The Gini coefficient measures wealth inequality and income concentration. The bottom 40 percent must achieve income growth faster than the national average. Wealth gap and wage inequality deprive lower-income households of economic security. Pro-poor growth policies target economic gains toward the poorest quintiles. Income share held by the richest concentrates political and economic power. Economic disparity between social classes undermines social cohesion and democratic participation. Addressing income inequality requires progressive fiscal policy and labour market reforms.

targets.description: Promote social, economic and political inclusion for all
targets.article: Social inclusion requires eliminating discrimination based on race, ethnicity, caste, disability, sexual orientation, and gender identity. Ethnic minorities and indigenous peoples face systematic exclusion from political, economic, and social life. Racial discrimination and ethnic exclusion deny equal rights and opportunities. LGBTQ rights and inclusion require legal protections and anti-discrimination enforcement. Disability rights and inclusion of disabled persons in mainstream society demand accessible infrastructure and legal protection. Marginalisation of social groups perpetuates poverty and denies human dignity. Inclusive societies actively protect and empower all people regardless of identity.

targets.description: Ensure equal opportunity and reduce inequality of outcomes
targets.article: Equal opportunity requires dismantling structural discrimination and systemic inequality embedded in laws, institutions, and social norms. Systemic racism denies equal access to education, employment, housing, and justice for racialised minorities. Social mobility — the ability to move up the economic ladder — is constrained by structural inequality across generations. Inequality of outcomes between social groups reflects unequal starting points and discriminatory treatment. Discrimination legislation prohibiting bias in hiring, housing, and services must be enforced. Reducing inequality of opportunity requires affirmative action, anti-discrimination law, and investment in marginalised communities.

targets.description: Adopt fiscal, wage and social protection policies for equality
targets.article: Fiscal, wage, and social protection policies directly determine inequality outcomes. Progressive taxation — higher taxes on the wealthy — reduces income concentration. Tax reform for equity and redistribution transfers resources from rich to poor. Wage policy including minimum wages and collective bargaining raises incomes for low-paid workers. Social protection for all provides a floor below which no one falls. Fiscal policy inequality can be addressed through spending on health, education, and transfers that reach the bottom. Inequality policy must combine revenue raising with targeted public expenditure benefiting marginalised populations.

targets.description: Improve regulation of financial markets
targets.article: Improved regulation and monitoring of financial markets reduces systemic risk and prevents crises that devastate developing country economies. Capital flow volatility destabilises currencies and asset markets in emerging economies. Global financial market oversight requires international coordination among regulators. Developing country finance regulation must protect against speculative attacks and contagion. Financial regulation strengthens banking systems and protects deposits. International financial architecture reform improves surveillance of cross-border capital flows and their impacts on vulnerable economies most exposed to global market fluctuations.

targets.description: Enhanced representation of developing countries in global institutions
targets.article: Developing countries are underrepresented in global governance institutions including the IMF, World Bank, WTO, and UN Security Council. Global governance reform must give emerging economies and least developed countries a stronger voice in decisions affecting them. IMF reform and World Bank governance changes improve developing country voting power and representation. Multilateral institution reform builds legitimacy and effectiveness. South-South cooperation and regional groupings amplify developing country positions in international negotiations. Equitable global governance produces fairer international trade, finance, and development rules.

targets.description: Facilitate orderly and responsible migration
targets.article: Safe, orderly, and regular migration serves both countries of origin and destination. Refugee protection and refugee rights require legal status, non-refoulement, and access to services. Migrant workers contribute to host economies while sending remittances home. Asylum seekers fleeing persecution need fair asylum systems and protection from deportation. Immigration policy must balance security concerns with humanitarian obligations. Migration governance frameworks coordinate international cooperation on safe migration. Irregular migration exposes people to exploitation and trafficking. Orderly migration channels reduce deaths, exploitation, and irregular flows.

targets.description: Implement special and differential treatment for developing countries
targets.article: Special and differential treatment for developing countries in WTO rules acknowledges structural asymmetries in global trade. Trade preferences and differential treatment allow least developed countries to face lower tariffs in major markets. WTO special treatment exempts developing countries from some obligations while they build capacity. Preferential trade access for least developed country exports supports their economic integration. Implementing differential treatment requires political commitment from developed countries to maintain preferential schemes. Trade preference utilisation by LDCs remains low due to rules of origin requirements and supply-side constraints.

targets.description: Encourage ODA flows to greatest need
targets.article: Official development assistance (ODA) flows to greatest need countries drive development in least developed nations. Development aid to high-need destinations — fragile states, landlocked developing countries, and small island states — closes financing gaps. Private investment in developing countries from foreign direct investment funds productive capacity. Aid for equality targets resources at reducing inequality within and between countries. Remittances from diaspora communities exceed ODA flows to many developing countries. Aligning ODA with need rather than strategic or commercial interests of donors improves development effectiveness.

targets.description: Reduce transaction costs of migrant remittances
targets.article: Migrant remittances are a lifeline for millions of families in developing countries. High remittance transaction costs — averaging 6-7 percent globally — erode funds reaching recipients. Reducing remittance costs to below 3 percent requires competition in money transfer markets and regulatory reform. Diaspora remittance flows are among the largest income sources for countries like the Philippines, India, and Mexico. Mobile money and digital transfer platforms are driving down remittance fees. Migrant remittance fee reduction requires removing exclusive partnerships and opening money transfer corridors to competition.

targets.description: Access to adequate, safe and affordable housing and slum upgrading
targets.article: Affordable housing is a human right denied by housing crises in cities across the globe. Slums, informal settlements, and shantytowns house a billion urban dwellers in substandard conditions without security or services. Housing shortages drive homelessness and forced evictions of vulnerable urban populations. Urban poverty concentrates in peripheral informal settlements lacking water, sanitation, and transport. Housing rights require legal protection against arbitrary eviction. Slum upgrading programmes provide security of tenure, infrastructure, and services in place. Affordable housing policies must combine supply expansion with protection of existing low-income communities.

targets.description: Sustainable transport systems for all
targets.article: Sustainable urban transport provides safe, affordable, and accessible mobility for all. Public transit — bus rapid transit (BRT), metro systems, urban rail, and light rail — reduces car dependence and emissions. Urban mobility planning integrates walking, cycling, and public transport. Road safety in cities protects pedestrians and cyclists from traffic deaths. Accessible public transport serves elderly, disabled, and low-income urban residents. Sustainable transport investment must prioritise mass transit over private vehicle infrastructure. Urban transport decarbonisation through electrification of buses and trains reduces city emissions significantly.

targets.description: Inclusive and sustainable urbanisation and participatory planning
targets.article: Inclusive and sustainable urbanisation requires integrated city planning and participatory governance. Urban planning and land use planning shape how cities grow and function. Urban sprawl wastes land and infrastructure while increasing commuting and emissions. Smart city technologies improve efficiency of urban services. Local government capacity for city governance determines quality of service delivery. Gentrification displaces poor residents from improving urban areas. Participatory urban planning involves communities in decisions affecting their neighbourhoods. Urban regeneration must benefit existing residents rather than driving displacement through land value increases.

targets.description: Protect and safeguard cultural and natural heritage
targets.article: Cultural heritage — historic buildings, archaeological sites, monuments, and intangible traditions — connects communities to their identity and history. UNESCO World Heritage Sites face threats from development, tourism, conflict, and climate change. Heritage protection and historic preservation require legal frameworks and dedicated funding. World Heritage Site designation provides international recognition and conservation support. Urban development must accommodate heritage preservation alongside economic growth. Cultural heritage tourism generates income while celebrating identity. Natural heritage including biodiversity hotspots and geological formations also requires protection from urban expansion and extractive industry.

targets.description: Reduce deaths and losses from disasters
targets.article: Natural disasters — floods, earthquakes, landslides, and cyclones — cause enormous loss of life and economic damage in cities. Urban flooding and city floods affect millions in coastal and riverside cities. Urban resilience and disaster risk reduction in cities requires flood defences, early warning, and evacuation plans. Disaster economic loss is concentrated in densely populated urban areas. Earthquake damage destroys housing and infrastructure in seismically active cities. Urban heat islands intensify heatwaves. Disaster mortality reduction requires resilient building codes, land use regulation excluding high-risk areas, and community preparedness.

targets.description: Reduce adverse environmental impact of cities
targets.article: Cities generate disproportionate air pollution, waste, and environmental degradation. Urban air quality and city air pollution — particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, and ozone — cause respiratory disease and premature death. Smog and industrial emissions in cities affect millions of urban residents. Municipal solid waste management — collection, sorting, and disposal — is a major urban challenge. Waste management and garbage collection services reach fewer residents in informal settlements. Reducing the environmental impact of cities requires clean transport, industrial regulation, and improved solid waste recycling and disposal infrastructure.

targets.description: Provide universal access to safe, inclusive green spaces
targets.article: Public parks, urban green spaces, and inclusive public spaces are essential for physical and mental wellbeing of urban residents. City parks provide recreation, cooling, air purification, and social gathering. Green infrastructure manages stormwater and reduces urban heat. Inclusive public space accommodates diverse users including women, children, elderly, and disabled people safely. Marginalised communities in dense urban areas often lack access to quality public space. Urban trees and parks deliver ecosystem services in cities. Planning for universal access to safe, green, and inclusive public spaces requires equitable investment across all urban neighbourhoods.

targets.description: Support positive economic, social and environmental links between urban and rural
targets.article: Linking urban and rural economies through regional planning creates more balanced development. Urban-rural linkages enable food supply chains, labour migration, and remittance flows that benefit both city and countryside. National urban policy frameworks integrate cities within broader regional development strategies. Regional planning coordinates infrastructure investment across urban and rural areas. Market towns and secondary cities mediate between rural producers and major urban markets. Positive economic links between urban centres and surrounding regions drive inclusive growth. Rural-urban migration requires cities to absorb populations sustainably with housing, services, and employment.

targets.description: Adopt integrated policies for inclusion, resource efficiency and resilience
targets.article: Integrated urban policies for climate resilience, resource efficiency, and inclusion build cities fit for the future. Sendai Framework implementation in urban areas requires cities to adopt disaster risk reduction plans. Urban disaster risk reduction incorporates flood mapping, building codes, and community early warning. City resilience strategies address climate change, inequality, and infrastructure gaps simultaneously. Resource efficiency policies reduce urban energy and water consumption. Integrated urban policy coordinates housing, transport, environment, and social development into coherent plans. Cities must adopt and implement comprehensive resilience strategies.

targets.description: Support least developed countries in sustainable building
targets.article: Sustainable and resilient building construction using local materials supports least developed countries (LDCs) in building urban infrastructure affordably. Green building design reduces energy and water consumption in new construction. Local material construction using stone, bamboo, and earth reduces costs and embodied carbon. Financial and technical assistance supports LDCs in adopting sustainable building standards. Sustainable building in fragile and conflict-affected settings requires simple, locally maintainable construction methods. Building codes that integrate climate resilience and energy efficiency must be adapted to developing country contexts and resource availability.

targets.description: Implement the 10-year sustainable consumption and production programme
targets.article: The 10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP) coordinates global policy action on consumption and production patterns. Sustainable consumption and production policy shifts economies from linear take-make-waste models. Sustainable lifestyles policy promotes lower-impact consumption choices through education and behaviour change. Production policy incentivises cleaner manufacturing and service delivery. Consumption policy reforms subsidies that drive unsustainable choices. Implementing the global sustainable consumption framework requires coordination among governments, businesses, and civil society across all sectors and regions.

targets.description: Sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources
targets.article: Natural resource management must use resources efficiently without exceeding planetary boundaries. Material footprint measures the total weight of raw materials extracted to serve an economy. Overconsumption in high-income countries drives global resource depletion and ecosystem degradation. Decoupling economic growth from resource use and environmental impact is the core sustainability challenge. Resource efficiency improves productivity while reducing waste. Unsustainable consumption of minerals, timber, water, and fossil fuels depletes stocks needed by future generations. Circular economy approaches keep resources in productive use longer.

targets.description: Halve global per capita food waste at retail and consumer levels
targets.article: Food waste and food loss account for one-third of all food produced globally. Consumer food waste in households and retail — supermarkets discarding edible produce — is highest in high-income countries. Post-harvest losses on farms and in supply chains dominate food loss in developing countries. Reducing food waste at retail and consumer levels halves waste per capita. Food spoilage from inadequate storage and cold chain failures causes significant losses. Food loss reduction requires infrastructure investment, consumer education, and retail incentive reform. Halving food waste saves resources, reduces emissions, and improves food security.

targets.description: Responsible management of chemicals and waste
targets.article: Responsible management of hazardous chemicals and waste protects human health and ecosystems. Chemical waste and toxic waste from industrial processes require safe disposal and treatment. E-waste and electronic waste are the fastest-growing waste stream globally, containing hazardous materials. The Basel Convention regulates transboundary movement of hazardous waste. The Rotterdam Convention manages chemical trade. Chemicals management frameworks identify and restrict toxic substances. Pesticide residues, industrial solvents, and heavy metals contaminate soils and waterways globally. Preventing chemical pollution requires stronger regulation, safer alternatives, and extended producer responsibility.

targets.description: Substantially reduce waste generation through prevention, reduction and recycling
targets.article: Plastic pollution chokes oceans, contaminates food chains, and degrades environments. Single-use plastic bans and plastic-free policies reduce waste at source. Plastic waste and microplastics accumulate in marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Recycling, upcycling, and composting divert materials from landfill. Waste reduction and zero waste policies prevent waste generation. Circular economy design keeps materials in productive use through repair, remanufacturing, and recycling loops. Textile waste and fast fashion waste generate massive volumes of discarded clothing.
