Preventing waste generation through product design, extended producer responsibility, and consumer behaviour change is prioritised over end-of-pipe management.

targets.description: Encourage companies to adopt sustainable practices and reporting
targets.article: Companies must adopt sustainable business practices and transparent sustainability reporting. Corporate social responsibility (CSR) and ESG reporting communicate environmental, social, and governance performance to investors and consumers. Sustainability reporting frameworks — GRI, TCFD, and ISSB standards — standardise corporate disclosure. Greenwashing — false or misleading environmental claims — undermines consumer trust and policy. Extended producer responsibility holds companies accountable for their products' end-of-life impacts. Right to repair legislation extends product lifespans. Sustainable business practices across supply chains reduce environmental impact of corporate activity.

targets.description: Sustainable public procurement practices
targets.article: Green procurement and sustainable public procurement align government purchasing with sustainability goals. Governments are the world's largest buyers — directing spending toward sustainable products and services drives market transformation. Eco-labels and product labelling enable consumers and procurement officers to identify environmentally preferable options. Supply chain transparency standards require companies to disclose supplier practices. Sustainable supply chains trace materials from source to consumer. Public procurement policy that favours local, low-carbon, and responsibly produced goods drives demand for sustainable production.

targets.description: Universal information and awareness for sustainable development
targets.article: Universal awareness and education about sustainable development empowers informed consumption choices. Consumer awareness of environmental impacts drives demand for sustainable products. Sustainable lifestyle campaigns promote reduced consumption, plant-based diets, and waste reduction. Green lifestyle choices — cycling, solar energy, repairing — reduce individual environmental footprint. Sustainability awareness in schools, workplaces, and communities builds culture of responsible consumption. Sustainable consumption education in curricula shapes values and behaviours of future generations. Information campaigns on product impacts and sustainability ratings guide purchasing decisions.

targets.description: Support developing countries to strengthen scientific and technological capacity
targets.article: Developing countries need scientific and technological capacity to shift toward sustainable production patterns. Green technology capacity enables local manufacturing of sustainable products and adoption of cleaner processes. Clean production capacity reduces industrial pollution and resource waste in emerging economies. Technology transfer for sustainable consumption supports low-income countries in leapfrogging polluting industries. Support for developing country industry to adopt energy-efficient, low-waste production methods requires finance, technology, and skills transfer. Building sustainability capacity in productive sectors drives green industrialisation.

targets.description: Develop and implement tools to monitor sustainable tourism impacts
targets.article: Sustainable tourism monitoring tools measure and manage the environmental, social, and economic impacts of tourism. Eco-friendly travel and responsible tourism certification reduce negative impacts on ecosystems and communities. Tourism impact assessment tools evaluate carbon footprint, biodiversity effects, and community benefits. Sustainable tourism policy requires monitoring frameworks that track carrying capacity and visitor impacts. Nature-based tourism and community-based tourism generate conservation revenue while minimising degradation. Tourism destinations need management plans that balance visitor access with ecosystem protection and local livelihood support.

targets.description: Rationalise inefficient fossil fuel subsidies
targets.article: Inefficient fossil fuel subsidies — government support for coal, oil, and gas — distort energy markets and encourage overconsumption of carbon-intensive energy. Fossil fuel subsidy reform removes price supports that subsidise polluting energy. Energy subsidy reform redirects public funds from fossil fuels to renewable energy and social protection. Coal subsidy, oil subsidy, and gas subsidy elimination sends price signals that encourage clean energy transition. Fuel subsidy reform is politically contentious as it raises energy costs for consumers. Progressive reform protects poor households from price increases while phasing out subsidies for the wealthy.

targets.description: Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate hazards
targets.article: Climate resilience and adaptive capacity protect communities from intensifying climate hazards. Heatwaves, extreme heat, and record temperatures stress health systems and agriculture. Flash floods, river flooding, coastal flooding, and storm surges destroy homes and livelihoods. Cyclones, hurricanes, typhoons, and tropical storms devastate coastal communities. Wildfires and forest fires destroy ecosystems and communities. Extreme droughts cut water and food supplies. Climate vulnerability and climate risk are highest in low-income countries. Climate refugees and climate displacement force populations from their homes. Building climate resilience requires infrastructure, early warning, and integrated adaptation planning.

targets.description: Integrate climate change measures into national policies
targets.article: Climate change, global warming, and the climate emergency demand urgent policy action. Greenhouse gas emissions and CO2 emissions from fossil fuels drive rising temperatures. Carbon footprint reduction, decarbonisation, and carbon neutrality are central policy objectives. The Paris Agreement commits countries to nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and net-zero targets. COP climate negotiations — COP26, COP27, COP28, COP29 — set global climate policy. Carbon pricing, carbon tax, and carbon markets make emissions costly. Carbon offsets and carbon credits fund emission reductions. IPCC climate science provides the evidence base for urgent action.

targets.description: Improve education, awareness and capacity on climate change
targets.article: Climate education, climate literacy, and public awareness are essential for building the social will to act on climate change. Climate capacity building enables governments, communities, and institutions to plan and implement adaptation and mitigation measures. Climate early warning systems provide timely alerts of extreme weather events. Integrating climate change into school curricula and professional training creates informed citizens and capable practitioners. Climate awareness campaigns mobilise public demand for policy action. Capacity development for climate planning strengthens national and local government ability to manage climate risks.

targets.description: Implement the UNFCCC commitment of $100 billion per year
targets.article: Climate finance is essential for developing countries to mitigate emissions and adapt to climate impacts. The $100 billion per year pledge by developed countries supports developing country climate action. The Green Climate Fund and climate investment mechanisms channel finance to vulnerable nations. Loss and damage compensation addresses irreversible climate impacts in small island states and least developed countries. Climate finance pledges have been partially fulfilled through bilateral and multilateral channels. Climate funding must scale dramatically beyond current levels. Climate compensation and loss and damage funds recognise historical responsibility of high-emission countries.

targets.description: Promote mechanisms for LDCs to plan and manage climate change
targets.article: Least developed countries (LDCs) and small island developing states (SIDS) face disproportionate climate vulnerability with minimal contribution to global emissions. SIDS climate threats — sea level rise, intensifying hurricanes, coral bleaching — threaten their very existence. LDC climate planning capacity building supports national adaptation planning and climate strategy development. Small island climate adaptation requires coastal protection, freshwater security, and livelihood diversification. International support for LDC and SIDS climate planning includes technical assistance, finance, and technology transfer tailored to their unique vulnerabilities and limited institutional capacities.

targets.description: Prevent and reduce marine pollution
targets.article: Marine pollution from plastic waste, oil spills, nutrient runoff, and land-based pollutants degrades ocean health. Ocean plastic and microplastics accumulate in marine food chains and harm marine life. Oil slicks and marine oil pollution from shipping and offshore extraction devastate coastal ecosystems. Nutrient runoff from agriculture causes algal blooms and oxygen-depleted dead zones in coastal waters. Plastic marine pollution enters from rivers and coastal dumping. Preventing and reducing marine pollution requires waste management on land, regulation of shipping emissions, and agricultural nutrient management.

targets.description: Sustainably manage and protect marine and coastal ecosystems
targets.article: Marine and coastal ecosystems — coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass meadows, and kelp forests — support extraordinary biodiversity and protect coastlines. Ocean health depends on managing fishing, pollution, coastal development, and climate impacts. Coral bleaching from warming ocean temperatures threatens coral reef systems globally. Marine conservation areas protect critical habitats. Blue carbon ecosystems — mangroves, seagrass, saltmarshes — sequester carbon and buffer coasts. Sustainable management of coastal habitat requires integrated coastal zone management. Marine biodiversity conservation is inseparable from climate action and pollution reduction.

targets.description: Minimize and address ocean acidification
targets.article: Ocean acidification from absorbed CO2 threatens marine ecosystems, particularly shell-forming organisms, corals, and marine food chains. Rising ocean temperature drives coral bleaching and species range shifts. Ocean warming disrupts marine productivity and ecosystem structure. Sea water chemistry changes reduce pH, dissolving the carbonate structures of shellfish, coral, and plankton. Addressing ocean acidification requires dramatic reduction of carbon emissions. The impacts of acidification on fisheries, aquaculture, and marine biodiversity are already measurable. Monitoring ocean chemistry tracks acidification progress and informs conservation strategies.

targets.description: Regulate harvesting and end overfishing
targets.article: Overfishing depletes fish stocks and threatens the livelihoods of fishing communities worldwide. Artisanal fishers, small-scale fishing communities, and fisherfolk depend on healthy fisheries for food and income. Illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing undermines management and strips resources from legal fishers. Fishing quotas, fishing licenses, and catch limits regulate sustainable harvest. Trawlers and bottom trawling damage seabed ecosystems and cause excessive bycatch. Depleted fish stocks require fishing bans and recovery periods. Sustainable fisheries management balances economic livelihoods with ecosystem health and long-term food security.

targets.description: Conserve at least 10 percent of coastal and marine areas
targets.article: Marine protected areas (MPAs) conserve biodiversity and allow fisheries to recover. Coastal conservation zones exclude destructive fishing and development from critical marine habitats. The 30x30 target — protecting 30 percent of oceans by 2030 — drives MPA expansion globally. Ocean conservation areas protect spawning grounds, feeding areas, and migration corridors. Effective MPA management requires surveillance, enforcement, and community engagement. High-seas marine protection on the open ocean requires international governance. Expanding ocean protection must balance conservation with the rights of fishing communities and coastal populations.

targets.description: Prohibit fisheries subsidies contributing to overfishing
targets.article: Fisheries subsidies that support overfishing and IUU fishing distort markets and accelerate stock depletion. WTO fisheries subsidies negotiations aim to discipline government support that contributes to overfishing and illegal fishing. Fishing subsidy reform would eliminate perverse incentives that allow fleets to fish profitably beyond sustainable catch limits. IUU fishing subsidy removal deprives operators of the financial support enabling illegal harvest. Reforming fishing subsidies protects small-scale fishers from unfair competition with heavily subsidised industrial fleets. International agreement on fisheries subsidy disciplines has been a long-running WTO priority.

targets.description: Increase economic benefits from sustainable use of marine resources
targets.article: The blue economy encompasses fisheries, aquaculture, marine tourism, shipping, and offshore energy. Sustainable use of marine resources generates economic value while maintaining ecosystem integrity. Fish farming and aquaculture produce a growing share of global seafood with lower wild catch pressure. Maritime economy jobs — fishing, fish processing, and marine services — sustain coastal livelihoods. Mariculture of shellfish, seaweed, and finfish provides sustainable seafood. Small island states and coastal nations depend on marine resources for food security and employment. Blue economy development must be grounded in ecosystem-based management.

targets.description: Increase scientific knowledge and marine technology
targets.article: Ocean science, marine research, and marine technology are essential for understanding and managing ocean ecosystems. Deep-sea exploration and seabed mapping reveal unknown biodiversity and resources. Deep-sea mining threatens fragile hydrothermal vent ecosystems and unknown species. Marine technology development enables sustainable aquaculture, fisheries monitoring, and pollution detection. Ocean knowledge from research institutions informs management decisions. Investing in marine research capacity in developing coastal nations builds local expertise. International scientific cooperation on ocean monitoring tracks biodiversity, temperature, acidification, and pollution trends.

targets.description: Provide access to marine resources for small-scale fishers
targets.article: Artisanal fishers and small-scale fishing communities must have secure access to marine resources, markets, and infrastructure. Traditional fishing communities face displacement by industrial fishing fleets and coastal development. Small-scale fishery rights require legal recognition in national fisheries law. Fishing port and harbour infrastructure serves small-scale fishers who cannot access distant industrial landing sites. Small fisher access to credit, equipment, and markets enables diversification and productivity improvement. Community management of coastal fisheries gives fisherfolk stewardship of resources they depend on.

targets.description: Enhance the conservation and sustainable use of oceans under UNCLOS
targets.article: UNCLOS — the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea — is the governing framework for maritime law and ocean governance. International maritime governance regulates shipping, fishing, mineral extraction, and conservation on the high seas. The BBNJ Agreement — the High Seas Treaty — extends marine protection beyond national jurisdiction. Coast guard operations and maritime safety protect vessels and enforce maritime law. Marine species — sea turtles, whales, dolphins, sharks, tuna, and manta rays — require international protection under conservation agreements. CITES regulates international trade in threatened marine species.

targets.description: Ensure conservation of terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems
targets.article: Terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems — forests, wetlands, peatlands, and mountain habitats — provide water, food, and biodiversity. National parks, protected areas, and nature reserves conserve ecosystems and wildlife. Wetland conservation and peatland protection store carbon and regulate water cycles. Freshwater ecosystem conservation supports aquatic biodiversity and water supply. Migratory birds and wildlife migration depend on intact habitat corridors. Alpine ecosystems face rapid change from warming temperatures. Terrestrial biodiversity conservation requires expanded and effectively managed protected areas across all major biomes.

targets.description: End deforestation and restore degraded forests
targets.article: Deforestation and forest degradation destroy biodiversity, release carbon, and threaten indigenous communities. Illegal logging and forest destruction drive tropical forest loss in the Amazon, Congo Basin, and Borneo. Amazon deforestation and rainforest loss are accelerating at alarming rates. Reforestation, afforestation, and tree planting restore forest cover and sequester carbon. Sustainable forest management balances timber production with conservation. Forest protection requires law enforcement against illegal clearing and incentives for conservation. REDD+ mechanisms pay developing countries for avoided deforestation.

targets.description: Combat desertification and restore degraded land
targets.article: Land degradation, soil erosion, and desertification reduce agricultural productivity and ecosystem services globally. Dryland agriculture is particularly vulnerable to land degradation. Land degradation neutrality — no net loss of productive land — guides national policy. Land restoration and land rehabilitation recover degraded soils through reforestation, erosion control, and improved farming practices. Soil degradation from overgrazing, chemical inputs, and compaction reduces agricultural output. Desertification in the Sahel, Central Asia, and dryland regions drives rural poverty and displacement. Restoring degraded land improves food security and climate resilience.

targets.description: Ensure conservation of mountain ecosystems
targets.article: Mountain ecosystems provide freshwater, biodiversity, and livelihoods for highland populations. Alpine and highland ecosystems are highly sensitive to climate change, with glaciers retreating and temperature regimes shifting. Glacier conservation matters for downstream water security. Mountain biodiversity includes endemic species found nowhere else. Altitude ecosystems from highlands to alpine zones harbour unique flora and fauna. Mountain communities depend on forest, pasture, and water resources. Conservation of mountain ecosystems requires protection from encroachment, overgrazing, and extractive activities that degrade fragile highland environments.

targets.description: Protect biodiversity and prevent extinction of threatened species
targets.article: Biodiversity loss and species extinction are accelerating at unprecedented rates. Habitat loss, deforestation, overexploitation, invasive species, and climate change drive the sixth mass extinction. Endangered and critically endangered species face extinction without conservation intervention. Threatened species require habitat protection, captive breeding, and legal protection from hunting and trade. Habitat fragmentation isolates wildlife populations, reducing genetic diversity. Wildlife habitat corridors connect fragmented protected areas. Biodiversity conservation demands both species-level protection and landscape-scale habitat management to halt ongoing extinction crisis.

targets.description: Fair and equitable sharing of genetic resources benefits
targets.article: Genetic resources — plant varieties, animal breeds, and microbial strains — are essential for agriculture, medicine, and industry. The Nagoya Protocol on access and benefit-sharing ensures communities and countries receive fair benefits from commercial use of their genetic resources and traditional knowledge. Access to traditional knowledge about plant uses must be governed with consent and benefit sharing. Benefit sharing from genetic resources supports conservation incentives. Biopiracy — unauthorized commercial exploitation of genetic resources — violates sovereignty and community rights. Implementing the Nagoya Protocol requires national legislation and monitoring systems.

targets.description: End poaching and trafficking of protected species
targets.article: Illegal wildlife trade and wildlife trafficking generate billions annually, devastating populations of elephants, rhinos, tigers, pangolins, and other threatened species. Poaching kills protected wildlife for ivory, horn, skin, and bushmeat. Wildlife crime networks traffic animals and animal parts through global criminal networks. Anti-poaching operations and wildlife rangers protect reserves. CITES regulates international trade in endangered species. Consumer demand in Asia for ivory, rhino horn, and exotic pets drives poaching pressure. Ending illegal wildlife trade requires demand reduction, law enforcement, and international cooperation to disrupt trafficking networks.

targets.description: Prevent and control invasive alien species
targets.article: Invasive alien species threaten native biodiversity on islands and in continental ecosystems. Non-native species introduced deliberately or accidentally can outcompete native species, disrupt food webs, and cause extinction. Island ecosystems are particularly vulnerable to invasive predators such as rats, cats, and snakes. Biosecurity measures at ports and borders prevent introduction of invasive species. Eradication and control of established invasive species is costly and technically demanding. Invasive species management requires international coordination on trade pathways and border controls to prevent introduction of harmful organisms.

targets.description: Integrate ecosystem values into national planning
targets.article: Ecosystem values must be integrated into national economic planning and decision-making. Natural capital accounting measures the economic value of ecosystem services — water purification, carbon sequestration, flood protection, and biodiversity. Ecosystem valuation makes visible the costs of environmental degradation. The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Kunming-Montreal framework set biodiversity finance and conservation targets. Payment for ecosystem services rewards landholders for maintaining forests, wetlands, and biodiversity. Biodiversity accounting in national accounts informs resource management decisions and nature finance mechanisms.

targets.description: Mobilise resources to conserve and sustainably use biodiversity
targets.article: Conserving and sustainably using biodiversity requires adequate and sustained financial resources. ODA for biodiversity and conservation funding from governments and philanthropies supports protected area management and restoration. Debt-for-nature swaps redirect debt repayments toward conservation. Payment for ecosystem services channels market revenues to conservation landholders. Biodiversity finance mechanisms mobilise private capital for nature conservation. Nature finance and nature-based solutions attract climate and biodiversity funding. Scaling conservation funding from billions to trillions requires innovative finance instruments beyond traditional development aid.

targets.description: Mobilise resources for sustainable forest management
targets.article: Sustainable forest management and halting deforestation require dedicated finance. REDD+ mechanisms compensate developing countries for reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation. Forest investment from governments, multilateral funds, and carbon markets funds conservation and sustainable forestry. Timber certification and sustainable forest supply chains generate premium prices for sustainably produced wood. Combating illegal logging requires enforcement funding, satellite monitoring, and trade regulations. Forest finance must reach forest-dependent communities and indigenous peoples who are the most effective forest stewards.

targets.description: Enhance support to combat poaching and trafficking
targets.article: Combating poaching and wildlife trafficking requires international support for enforcement, community conservation, and demand reduction. Wildlife crime enforcement agencies and park rangers need equipment, training, and salaries to protect threatened species. Anti-poaching operations require intelligence networks and international law enforcement cooperation. Community conservation engages local people as wildlife stewards through benefit-sharing and livelihood alternatives. Ranger benefit programmes improve ranger welfare and retention. Ending wildlife trafficking demands prosecution of criminal networks, consumer demand reduction, and addressing poverty driving poaching in source communities.

targets.description: Reduce all forms of violence and related death rates
targets.article: Armed conflict, civil war, political violence, and terrorism kill hundreds of thousands annually and displace millions. War crimes, genocide, and ethnic cleansing represent the gravest violations of international law. Airstrikes, shelling, missile attacks, and military operations cause civilian casualties in conflict zones. Peace agreements, ceasefire deals, and peace negotiations seek to end hostilities. Armed groups, militias, and insurgencies fuel protracted conflicts. Violence reduction and homicide rate decline require law enforcement, social investment, and conflict resolution. Peace processes must address root causes of conflict.

targets.description: End abuse, exploitation, trafficking and all violence against children
targets.article: Violence and abuse against children — physical, sexual, and psychological — violates their rights and scars development. Child trafficking and trafficking of children across borders for exploitation and labour is a grave human rights crime. Child soldiers recruited by armed groups suffer trauma and loss of childhood. Sexual exploitation of children — including online abuse and child prostitution — demands urgent action by justice systems and technology companies. Child protection systems in schools, health services, and communities must identify and respond to abuse. Ending violence against children requires legal frameworks, reporting mechanisms, and social norm change.

targets.description: Promote the rule of law and ensure equal access to justice
targets.article: Rule of law and equal access to justice are foundations of peaceful, inclusive societies. Judicial independence protects courts from political interference. Legal aid and access to justice services ensure the poor can pursue rights in court. Impunity for human rights violations must be overcome through accountability and prosecution. Extrajudicial killing and police brutality violate the right to life and due process. Transitional justice mechanisms — truth commissions, reparations — address past atrocities. Prison conditions and torture in detention violate human rights. Functional court systems with professional judges are essential for rule of law.

targets.description: Reduce illicit financial and arms flows and strengthen asset recovery
targets.article: Organised crime, drug trafficking, arms trafficking, and money laundering generate illicit financial flows that corrupt governments and fund conflict. Drug cartels control territories and governments in some countries through violence and bribery. Arms trafficking supplies conflict zones with weapons despite international embargoes. Illicit financial flows through money laundering, tax havens, and corrupt asset transfers deprive states of development resources. Sanctions regimes target arms dealers and financial criminals. Asset recovery mechanisms return stolen funds to affected countries. Fighting organised crime requires international law enforcement cooperation and financial intelligence.

targets.description: Substantially reduce corruption and bribery
targets.article: Corruption — bribery, embezzlement, and abuse of public office — undermines governance, economic development, and public trust. Anti-corruption measures include independent oversight institutions, transparent procurement, and asset disclosure requirements. Kleptocracy and state capture by corrupt elites redirect public resources to private gain. Graft in public contracts diverts funds from services to kickbacks. Whistleblowers exposing corruption face retaliation and must be legally protected. International anti-corruption cooperation freezes and recovers stolen assets. Corrupt officials must face prosecution to deter future abuse. Anti-graft institutions require independence and adequate resources.

targets.description: Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions
targets.article: Effective, accountable, and transparent government institutions are prerequisites for sustainable development. Democratic governance ensures citizens can hold leaders accountable through elections, oversight, and free press. Authoritarian governments and democratic backsliding undermine rights and institutional accountability. Electoral fraud and election rigging delegitimise democratic systems. Accountable institutions require public financial management, audit systems, and open contracting. Public administration reform improves government effectiveness and service delivery. Transparent governance reduces corruption and improves public trust. Citizens must be able to access information about government decisions and spending.

targets.description: Ensure inclusive participatory and representative decision-making
targets.article: Inclusive, participatory, and representative decision-making strengthens governance legitimacy. Civil society participation in policy processes ensures diverse voices shape decisions. Democratic participation enables citizens to engage with governance beyond voting. Political inclusion of women, minorities, and marginalised groups in representative bodies improves policy quality. Participatory decision-making in community development, urban planning, and resource management builds ownership. Representative democracy requires independent electoral commissions and open political competition. Inclusive governance outcomes depend on removing barriers that prevent underrepresented groups from participating in political processes.

targets.description: Broaden and strengthen participation of developing countries in global governance
targets.article: Developing countries are chronically underrepresented in global governance bodies. UN Security Council reform to reflect contemporary power realities has been blocked by permanent members. Multilateral participation of developing countries in trade, finance, and climate negotiations requires capacity and political will from powerful states. G20 and G7 decisions affect all countries but are made by a few. Developing country representation in international financial institutions, standards bodies, and regulatory agencies must be increased. Global governance reform would produce more legitimate, effective, and equitable international institutions.

targets.description: Provide legal identity for all including birth registration
targets.article: Legal identity is a prerequisite for accessing education, health, financial, and government services. Birth registration establishes legal identity from birth. Statelessness — lacking nationality and legal identity — leaves millions without rights or protection. Civil registration systems record births, deaths, and marriages. Documentation — identity cards, passports, and certificates — enables people to exercise their rights. Undocumented populations are invisible to governments and excluded from services. Providing legal identity for all requires investment in civil registration infrastructure and outreach to marginalised communities.

targets.description: Ensure public access to information and fundamental freedoms
targets.article: Press freedom and freedom of expression enable accountability and informed citizenship. Journalists killed, imprisoned, and threatened cannot report on corruption and human rights violations. Media freedom is under attack globally with censorship, defamation laws, and direct violence against reporters. Disinformation and propaganda undermine public trust in factual reporting. Freedom of information laws enable citizens to access public records and government decisions. Political prisoners detained for expression violate rights to speech and conscience. Human rights violations require transparent investigation, accountability, and protection for victims and witnesses.

targets.description: Strengthen national institutions to prevent violence and terrorism
targets.article: Preventing violence, terrorism, and extremism requires strong national institutions with adequate capacity. Counter-terrorism efforts must balance security with human rights protection. Security institution reform builds professional, accountable police and military forces. Violence prevention programmes address root causes — poverty, exclusion, and grievance — that fuel radicalisation and recruitment. National security capacity building supports fragile states in maintaining order and protecting civilians. Terrorism financing disruption cuts resources for violent extremist organisations. Community-based violence prevention and social cohesion programmes reduce conflict risk.

targets.description: Promote and enforce non-discriminatory laws and policies
targets.article: Non-discriminatory laws and policies protect all people from discrimination based on race, gender, religion, and other identity characteristics. Human rights legislation codifies fundamental protections and enables judicial enforcement. Equality laws prohibiting discrimination in employment, housing, education, and services must be comprehensive and enforced. Anti-discrimination policy backed by strong institutions protects minority groups from systemic bias. Non-discriminatory governance applies laws equally regardless of social status, political affiliation, or identity. Universal human rights standards require governments to enact and enforce non-discriminatory legal frameworks.

targets.description: Strengthen domestic resource mobilisation
targets.article: Domestic resource mobilisation through effective tax collection is the foundation of sustainable development finance. Tax revenue and public revenue generation in developing countries must grow to fund services and investment. Fiscal capacity building improves tax administration and reduces evasion. Tax system development in least developed countries requires institutional support and technology. Broadening the tax base and improving tax compliance increases public revenue. Domestic resource mobilisation reduces aid dependence and builds accountability between governments and citizens. Progressive tax reform raises revenue while reducing inequality.

targets.description: Developed countries implement ODA commitments
targets.article: Developed countries committed to providing 0.7 percent of GNI as official development assistance (ODA). Most donor countries have not met this commitment. ODA flows fund development programmes in education, health, agriculture, and governance. Development aid channelled bilaterally and multilaterally supports least developed countries. Aid commitments must be honoured and aid effectiveness improved through country ownership and alignment with national priorities. Bilateral aid and multilateral aid complement each other. Foreign aid remains critical for the poorest countries despite growing private capital flows.

targets.description: Mobilise additional financial resources for developing countries
targets.article: Mobilising additional financial resources for developing countries from multiple sources is essential. Development finance from blended finance mechanisms combines public and private capital for development impact. Development funding through foreign direct investment (FDI) builds productive capacity. Humanitarian aid addresses immediate crises while development aid funds long-term investment. Aid disbursement and aid effectiveness determine whether finance reaches intended beneficiaries. Private finance for developing countries must be attracted through de-risking instruments, guarantees, and enabling policy environments that reduce investment barriers.

targets.description: Assist developing countries in attaining long-term debt sustainability
targets.article: Developing country debt sustainability is threatened by high debt burdens and rising interest rates. Debt relief and debt restructuring provide breathing space for heavily indebted poor countries (HIPC). Sovereign debt crises in developing countries require coordinated international response. Debt sustainability analysis guides borrowing decisions and creditor assessments. Debt swaps exchange debt obligations for investments in development or nature conservation. HIPC initiative and MDRI debt relief programmes reduced debt burdens for the poorest. New debt crises in developing countries demand updated international debt resolution frameworks.

targets.description: Adopt and implement investment promotion regimes
targets.article: Investment promotion regimes attract foreign direct investment to least developed countries and developing economies. LDC investment frameworks provide incentives, legal protections, and business environment improvements for foreign investors. Investment promotion agencies market countries' investment opportunities and streamline regulatory approvals. FDI regimes in developing countries must balance investor protection with development priorities. Investment framework development improves rule of law, contract enforcement, and dispute resolution. Attracting productive FDI requires stable macroeconomic conditions, infrastructure, and skills.

targets.description: Enhance knowledge sharing and cooperation on science and technology
targets.article: Knowledge sharing and cooperation on science, technology, and innovation accelerate sustainable development. South-South cooperation transfers knowledge and technology between developing countries. Triangular cooperation involves a facilitating developed country supporting South-South exchanges. North-South cooperation channels technology and expertise from advanced to developing economies. International knowledge sharing platforms and technology access schemes reduce technological divides. Science and technology cooperation agreements build research partnerships. Sharing scientific knowledge freely accelerates progress on shared global challenges.

targets.description: Promote development, transfer and dissemination of environmentally sound technologies
targets.article: Developing countries need access to environmentally sound technologies to industrialise sustainably. Technology transfer from advanced to developing economies enables leapfrogging of polluting technologies. Clean technology transfer supports green industrialisation, renewable energy adoption, and sustainable agriculture. Intellectual property barriers to technology transfer must be reduced for least developed countries. Environmentally sound technology access requires international agreements, licensing provisions, and financial support. Promoting technology transfer for clean energy, water treatment, and sustainable agriculture supports multiple sustainable development goals simultaneously.

targets.description: Fully operationalise technology bank for LDCs
targets.article: The Technology Bank for LDCs provides dedicated institutional support for technology access and innovation capacity in least developed countries. LDC technology development requires investments in education, infrastructure, and institutional capacity. ICT capacity building in LDCs enables digital economy participation. Least developed country internet access and digital connectivity are prerequisites for modern development. Technology bank for LDCs operations include technology brokering, capacity building, and research networking. Operationalising the Technology Bank requires sustainable funding and active engagement from technology-exporting countries.

targets.description: Enhance international support for capacity building
targets.article: Capacity building and technical assistance strengthen developing countries' ability to plan and implement sustainable development. Capacity development covers institutional strengthening, skills training, and systems building across government and civil society. International support for capacity building funds training programmes, secondments, and institutional partnerships. Development capacity in public administration, statistics, planning, and finance management improves governance quality. Technical assistance from multilateral agencies provides expertise on complex policy challenges. Sustainable capacity development builds local institutions rather than creating aid dependency.

targets.description: Promote universal rules-based multilateral trading system
targets.article: A universal, rules-based, open, non-discriminatory multilateral trading system under WTO rules underpins global prosperity. Multilateral trade negotiations under the Doha Development Agenda sought to improve developing country market access. WTO rules-based trading system prevents discriminatory and arbitrary trade measures. Non-discriminatory trade principles apply equally to all members. Equitable trade rules level the playing field for developing country exporters. Dispute resolution through WTO mechanisms protects smaller economies from powerful trading partners' unilateral actions. Multilateralism in trade governance is more equitable than bilateral power dynamics.

targets.description: Increase exports of developing countries
targets.article: Developing country export share in world trade must increase for them to benefit from globalisation. LDC exports face barriers in major markets from tariffs, standards, and non-tariff measures. Market access for developing country exports drives foreign exchange earnings and economic growth. Export diversification beyond raw commodities adds value and stability. Developing country export competitiveness requires investment in productivity, quality standards, and trade infrastructure. Increasing the share of global exports from developing countries requires both supply-side improvements and market opening by major importing nations.

targets.description: Duty-free and quota-free market access for LDCs
targets.article: Duty-free and quota-free market access for least developed country exports removes tariff barriers in major markets. LDC trade preferences are granted by developed countries under the Everything But Arms initiative, GSP, and similar schemes. Trade preference utilisation by LDCs requires rules of origin compliance and supply capacity to export. Quota-free access for LDC agricultural and textile exports is particularly important for poor countries. Preferential market access for least developed countries is a global commitment that must be maintained and deepened to support development through trade.

targets.description: Enhance global macroeconomic stability
targets.article: Global macroeconomic stability enables sustained development and reduces financial crises that devastate developing economies. Policy coordination among major economies prevents competitive devaluations and trade wars. Global economy coordination addresses spillovers from monetary policy in advanced economies on developing countries. Macroeconomic stability requires coordinated fiscal, monetary, and exchange rate policies. IMF surveillance and policy dialogue support macroeconomic stability. Global financial crises originating in advanced economies spread rapidly to developing countries through trade and financial channels. Systemic risk management requires collective action.

targets.description: Enhance policy coherence for sustainable development
targets.article: Policy coherence for sustainable development ensures that trade, finance, agriculture, and environment policies reinforce rather than undermine development goals. Development coherence requires that rich country policies do not harm developing countries through unfair trade rules, tax havens, or arms exports. Policy coordination across government departments aligns incentives with sustainable development. Coherent development policy eliminates contradictions between aid programmes and harmful commercial policies. Policy space for developing countries to pursue own strategies must be respected. Monitoring policy coherence holds governments accountable for development impacts of their domestic policies.

targets.description: Respect national leadership for sustainable development policies
targets.article: Respecting national leadership and policy space for sustainable development allows countries to choose their own strategies based on their circumstances. Country ownership of development plans improves sustainability and accountability. Policy space for developing countries to use industrial policy, capital controls, and trade measures must be protected in international agreements. National leadership development strategies should be supported, not undermined, by donors and investors. Development effectiveness principles — ownership, alignment, harmonisation — support country-led development. International partners must respect sovereignty while promoting accountability and transparency.

targets.description: Enhance multi-stakeholder partnerships for sustainable development
targets.article: Multi-stakeholder partnerships for sustainable development mobilise knowledge, finance, and innovation from governments, business, and civil society. Global partnerships and international partnerships align diverse actors around shared development goals. Public-private partnerships leverage private sector finance and expertise for public goods. UN partnership frameworks coordinate multilateral system support. Multilateral cooperation on climate, health, trade, and technology requires effective governance of partnership mechanisms. Multi-stakeholder platforms enable inclusive dialogue on global challenges. International partnerships must be results-oriented, transparent, and accountable to intended beneficiaries.

targets.description: Encourage effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships
targets.article: Public-private partnerships (PPPs) combine government authority and private capital to finance and deliver infrastructure and services. Civil society collaboration ensures development programmes reflect community needs and rights. Effective partnerships between governments, businesses, and NGOs deliver better outcomes than single-actor approaches. Blended finance partnerships attract private investment to development projects by reducing risk. Public-private partnership models for water, energy, transport, and health infrastructure mobilise private capital for public goods. Governance of partnerships must prevent private interests from overriding public development objectives.

targets.description: Enhance data, monitoring and statistics capacity
targets.article: High-quality, disaggregated data and statistics are essential for monitoring sustainable development progress. Statistical capacity in developing countries enables evidence-based policy and accountability. Data availability for developing countries on income, health, education, and environment is inadequate. Disaggregated data by gender, age, disability, and geography ensures no one is left behind in monitoring. SDG data frameworks track progress on all 17 goals and 169 targets. National statistics offices need investment in systems, skills, and independence. Monitoring and statistics capacity building supports effective development planning.

targets.description: Build on existing initiatives to measure progress beyond GDP
targets.article: Measuring development progress beyond GDP requires new statistical tools and frameworks. Alternative welfare measures capture wellbeing, inequality, and sustainability beyond income. Census data and household surveys provide comprehensive socioeconomic data. National accounts modernisation integrates natural capital and social progress indicators. Statistical capacity building supports developing country ability to produce and use quality data. Progress measurement innovation — human development index, multidimensional poverty index — supplements GDP. Building robust national statistical systems enables genuine monitoring of sustainable development outcomes and informs responsive policy.
